issues: Sales reached target, supported by tourists and regular customers, and covers rose, but spend per head fell because of loyalty app subscribers, free items and voucher users.
Labour was held down by sending staff on breaks during quiet periods, although kitchen hours, especially for one trainee, still need to be saved methodically.
A Deliveroo missing item claim for a salmon avocado roll was disputed with photo evidence that the full order was handed to the driver, and Deliveroo accepted the dispute.
Deliveroo late prep orders were raised, and sushi bar prep timing and package photos need tightening.
Kobas keeps showing completed invoices as pending for several weeks, and invoice management and communication from the kitchen side still need improving.
Five star Google reviews increased after active staff engagement; the low star reviews concerned food quality, confusion over side dishes being served as starters, and vouchers.
Front of house need more check backs, better guest feedback checks and faster service with fewer mistakes; back of house need to focus on dish cleanliness and food quality.
Waste ran high for the week; all waste was recorded and back of house need to monitor food cost and waste more closely.
Severe mould and damp odours in the downstairs area and toilets led to a proposal for dehumidifiers, air purifiers and room scent diffusers.

Maintenance log: blocked ladies toilets, a leaking VIP room, a leaking bar and the baby changing unit are urgent; the men's toilet tap and entrance and toilet flooring are medium priority, all with Francheska or Ross.
The kitchen floor repair, logged about a month ago, has still not been done and is being logged again; the stair handrail has been fixed.
Deep cleaning of the sushi bar and bar is done, with weekly Sunday cleaning, pest monitoring and kitchen labelling procedures still needing focus.

Influencers with small followings are booking tables for two, bringing larger groups and ordering heavily without meaningful promotional value, and a group event booked for 25 brought 40 guests who stayed five hours with low spend; the site has sent a formal letter to marketing asking for stricter caps.

Staffing: two part time front of house hires have joined, an AGM has transferred in from Leeds, a sushi chef has been hired, and a front of house role of around 25 hours is being recruited through interviews and trial shifts.
A hot section chef leaves for three months from 24/10 until January, so a new hire is being trained by him to cover.
A kitchen team member is training on sushi, invoices and stock management.
Staff feel salaries are below London and Central London standards and are asking for a higher rate.
Live promotions are the loyalty app, influencer bookings, Freshers and the discount platforms; the site will distribute sushi at the Freshers festival in Islington.
Region-wide (South England): Staff must explicitly confirm pork ingredients and dietary requirements with customers when taking orders, rather than making assumptions from appearance.
Region-wide (South England): Right to work checks must be fully cleared before any new starter is scheduled for a shift.
